description: The input closure for every Axiom module the New Zealand v0 graph binds: each root input of each module's committed input surface is encoded (by a concept binding of the axiom:nz mapping, a state binding declared here, or another graph node), or defaulted with its reason and citation. The axiom adapter omits an input the frame lacks, and the engine fails a request that reaches an absent input, so a run feeds every entry here. The defaults are modelling content listed for the D1 method review.
status: awaiting D1: every default is a proposal (new_default true)

rulespec_pin.note: The input surface was generated at 6fe181fc, an ancestor of the MC1 pin 8dc2507; git log 6fe181fc..8dc2507 lists no commit touching the four modules, and their SHA-256 values below are the same at both.

receipt_flags.note: The person-level receipt flags the receipt layer (takeup.assign@1) writes and the state bindings read. Their names are a contract with that kernel.

receipt_requirements.note: What the receipt layer (takeup.assign@1) must enforce because the closure's entitlement defaults leave it to receipt. Each is a modelling default for D1.
requirements: At most one main benefit (Jobseeker Support, Sole Parent Support, Supported Living Payment) per person: Social Security Act 2018 s 18; main_benefit_receiving_another_main_benefit is defaulted false.
Never New Zealand Superannuation and a main benefit for the same person: s 18; main_benefit_receiving_new_zealand_superannuation is defaulted false on transported frames.

A main benefit only where the rates module's income-tested net weekly payment for it is positive: entitlement treats the s 24 income test and the s 21 work gap as met (jobseeker_income_less_than_zero_rate_cutout true, jobseeker_in_full_time_employment false), and the Sole Parent Support and Supported Living Payment entitlement rules have no income term; the rates module tests the person's own income only.

engine_optional_evidence: axiom-rules-engine 04315d94 (the engine that generated the committed input surface) has no optional inputs. A RuleSpec module has no inputs section (RulesDocument holds format, imports, module, units, relations and rules; src/rulespec.rs:361-374), a rule-level default is rejected (RuleSpecError::UnsupportedDefault, src/rulespec.rs:91-94), and the dense batch call collects only the inputs the caller supplies (python-ext/src/lib.rs:458-466). A plain read of an absent input fails every row whose evaluation reaches it with EvalError::MissingInput (src/dense.rs:2790-2803), and that fails the request. The internal input_or_else node that would read a default (src/dense.rs:2805-2811) is never produced from RuleSpec text: formula lowering turns a name no rule defines into a plain input read (src/formula.rs:1400-1413). So no root input of these modules can be verified engine-optional, and this closure classes none as such: an input a run does not encode is defaulted here, with its reason.

undetermined_judgments.reason: Entitlement judgments come back as codes 1 (holds), -1 (does not hold) and 0 (undetermined). At axiom-rules-engine 04315d94 no dense leaf yields an undetermined value: dense input columns are booleans, integers, floats or text, an absent input is an error rather than an unknown, and and/or/not only pass an undetermined item along. With every root input encoded or defaulted by this closure, a 0 cannot arise, so takeup.assign@1 refuses any 0 it sees instead of guessing: a 0 would mean the engine or the closure changed. The alternatives a review could choose are treating 0 as not entitled (understates receipt) or as entitled (overstates it). microcosm.frame.input_closure.resolve_judgments implements all three.

knobs.name: rent_allocation
knobs.note: A household's rent goes to the family containing the reference person (central, a lower bound for other families), or is shared among the household's families in proportion to their adults (scenario S2, the upper sensitivity). Either way the families' rents sum to the household's.

knobs.name: asset_test
knobs.note: On (central): each family's summed liquid financial assets meet the reg 15 cash-asset limits. Off (scenario S1, an upper bound): every family's cash assets are set to zero, so the limit never binds.

knobs.name: area_column
knobs.note: Which household area assignment the area flags read: the central crosswalk (as_area) or the alternative (as_area_alt, scenario S3).

knobs.name: rent_factor
knobs.note: A factor on every family's weekly rent: 1.0 centrally; scenario S4's stock adjustment from lodged-bond rents to all rents takes its factor from the B6 evidence.

The Treasury IncomeExplorer reproduction harness defaults it the same way (TheAxiomFoundation ops nz-lane/emtr_reproduction/run.py, ModelEvaluator.accommodation_values).
